paper.title: Stealthy Adversarial Attacks on Stochastic Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Reward poisoning (targeted) attacks on stochastic MAB with homogeneity-test attack detection
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Main guarantees are for the attacker (number of target-arm pulls forced, attack cost, stealthiness) and for detection, not regret guarantees of the learner.
unmapped: Targeted attack objective: attacker wants the target arm pulled T-o(T) times with o(T) cost
Learner runs a homogeneity-test attack detector with public parameter delta
Stealthiness constraint on the attacker (detection probability at most delta)
settings.definition_quote: a bandit game consists of $N$ arms with unknown but fixed $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian reward distributions ... At each round $t$ after the learner chooses to play arm $I_{t}$, the attacker manipulates the reward into $r_{t}=r_{t}^{0}-\alpha_{t}$ ... we consider the attack successful if after $T$ rounds the attacker spends $o(T)$ cumulative attack cost and forces the learner to choose the target arm for $T-o(T)$ times.

algorithms.name: Constructed learning algorithm with special actions (UCB1-based) and matching stealthy attack

source.label: lemma: detection error
source.quote: The probability of the union of all the type-I errors introduced by Eq.\eqref{eq:hyp-test} can be upper bounded by $\delta$.

results.notes: Type-I error of the detection test.

symbols.Delta0: realized first reward of arm 1 minus mean of target arm, hat mu_1(N) - mu_target
symbols.beta1: beta(1, delta), detection confidence width at n=1

conditions: attack not detected in the history
tuning: UCB bonus 3 sigma sqrt(log t / N_i)

source.label: lemma: UCB1 unattackable
source.quote: Suppose the learner runs the UCB1 algorithm to choose arms. For any history of pulls $\mathcal{H}_{T}$ where the attack is not detected, if $\Delta^{0}_{1K}>\beta(1)$, with probability at least $1-\frac{1}{T^{3}}$ the number of rounds that target arm $K$ is pulled up to time $T$: $N_{K}(T)$ is bounded by ...

results.notes: Bound on number of target-arm pulls (quantity other). Paper's N (arms) mapped to K.

conditions: probability at least 1 - eta - 2(Delta0-beta1)^7/(7(9 sigma^2 log T)^{7/2})

source.label: theorem: UCB1 attack
source.quote: Suppose the learner applies the UCB1 algorithm. If $\Delta^{0}_{1K} < \beta(1)$, with probability at least $1 - \eta - \frac{2(\Delta^{0}_{1K}-\beta(1))^{7}}{7(9\sigma^{2}\log T)^{\frac{7}{2}}}$, the attacker forces the learner to choose the target arm in at least $T-\left(\frac{9\sigma^{2}}{(\Delta^{0}_{1K}-\beta(1))^2}+\frac{9N\sigma^{2}}{d^2}\right)\log T -(N-1)$ rounds...

results.notes: Recorded as an upper bound on the number of non-target pulls (T minus target pulls).

symbols.sum_D: sum over arms i != 1, target of |mu_1 - mu_i|

conditions: probability at least 1 - eta - 2(Delta0-beta1)^7/(7(9 sigma^2 log T)^{7/2})

source.quote: ... and incurs a cumulative attack cost at most (\frac{18(\beta(1)+\beta(1, \eta))\sigma^{2}}{(\Delta^{0}_{1K}-\beta(1))^{2}} + ...)\log T + ...

results.notes: Cumulative attack cost bound for the stealthy attack (stealthy by Lemma 5).

source.quote: Suppose the learner applies the same $\epsilon$-greedy algorithm as in Lemma \ref{lemma: epsilon unattackable}. If $\Delta^{0}_{1K} < \beta(1)$, with probability at least $1 - 3\eta$, the attacker forces the learner to choose the target arm in at least $ T - t_{2} - N(...)$ rounds...

source.label: lemma: construction
source.quote: We can find a learning algorithm such that given any sub-Gaussian environment $(F_{1},\cdots, F_{N})$, the number of arm pulls of any sub-optimal arm $i$ follows $E(N_{i}(T)) = \Theta(\log T)$, and simultaneously the attacker can find a corresponding stealthy attack method ...

results.notes: Expected pulls of each suboptimal arm for constructed algorithm.

conditions: target arm pulled T - O(log T) times

source.label: lemma: construction
source.quote: ... for any target arm $K \in \{1,\cdots, N\}$ with probability at least $1-\eta$ the attacker can force the learner to choose the target arm for $T-O(\log T)$ times with a cumulative attack cost at most $O(\log T \sqrt{\log (\frac{1}{\eta})})$.

results.notes: Attack cost bound of stealthy attack against constructed algorithm; Lemma 7 gives the same for an ERR algorithm.
